name: Layer
tagline: Browser platform for generating and refining game and marketing art, 3D, video and audio.
best_for: Game studios and content teams producing assets at scale
description:
Layer is a browser-based platform where game and marketing teams generate and refine creative assets in one place. It covers 2D art, 3D, video and audio, and includes a canvas editor, upscaling, vector conversion and background removal, so an asset does not have to bounce between several separate apps.

Teams can save style libraries and workflows and reuse them, and the listing says these carry over when you switch models. Bulk refinement helps when you have a whole batch of characters or ad variations to clean up. A Unity plugin and CSV import and export are mentioned, along with security controls such as role-based access and audit logs. Plans are credit-based, so check the official site for current limits and pricing.
use_steps: Create a workspace and open the canvas.
Generate or upload a first batch of assets.
Refine them with upscaling, background removal or batch tools.
Save the style as a reusable workflow and export in the format your engine needs.

cons: Credit-based usage can be hard to forecast
Aimed at teams, so solo hobbyists may not need most of it
features: Upscaling, vector conversion and background removal
use_cases: Producing character art for a game
Cleaning up asset batches before engine import
pricing_details: A free plan with a limited number of creative units is mentioned, with paid tiers adding more usage and enterprise features. Plans change, so check the official site for current details.

faq.a: 2D images, 3D, video and audio, according to its listing.

name: Ludo.ai
tagline: AI assistant for game ideation, market research and narrative content.
best_for: Indie developers and studios in the concept stage
description:
Ludo.ai is a cloud tool aimed at the earliest stages of game development. From text prompts it can produce game concepts, characters, mechanics and level ideas, and it can write quests and dialogue to flesh out a story.

It also includes market research features such as trend and competitor analysis, which helps when deciding whether a concept is worth building. Guided workflows are meant to make it usable by people who are not technical, and real-time collaboration supports distributed teams. It runs in the browser, and mentions of integrations with analytics, collaboration and engine workflows are on its listing. It is described as a subscription product with possible trials rather than a permanent free tool, so check the official site for what is on offer.

name: Modl.ai
tagline: AI bots that playtest games and report bugs.
best_for: QA teams and developers who want automated playtesting
description:
Modl.ai provides AI bots that play your game to find problems. They run simulated playthroughs, explore levels, spot bugs and performance issues, and model how players behave, which takes some repetitive load off manual QA.

Player simulation can also inform balancing of difficulty and progression. The service connects to Unity, Unreal and custom engines through SDKs and APIs, and an analytics dashboard shows test coverage and bug trends. Cloud-based, it can run many bot sessions across builds and platforms, including mobile, PC and console titles. Pricing is described as primarily enterprise, with some partners offering trials, so contact the official site for current terms.
use_steps: Integrate the SDK into your Unity, Unreal or custom build.
Configure bots and test goals.
Run sessions in the cloud across builds.
Review bugs and coverage in the dashboard.
pros: Dashboard for coverage and bug trends
cons: Enterprise-style pricing may not suit tiny teams

name: Promethean AI
tagline: World-building assistant that speeds up 3D scene assembly.
description:
Promethean AI helps artists assemble 3D scenes faster. It works alongside the tools they already use, surfacing assets and offering layout and style suggestions based on context instead of replacing the modelling software.

Metadata-driven search finds references, materials and models in large asset libraries. Plugins are listed for Unreal Engine, Unity, Maya and Blender, with an API for custom pipelines and permission, encryption and audit controls for teams. Uses mentioned include cinematic environments, product visualizations and interactive worlds. It is described as primarily paid with studio options, and a demo has been referenced, so confirm current availability on the official site.

name: Kavout
tagline: AI stock research platform built around the Kai Score ranking.
best_for: Retail traders and advisors researching US equities
description:
Kavout is an investing research platform that blends fundamentals, price data and alternative datasets into ranked stock ideas and written analysis. Its core is the Kai Score, a machine-learning rating from 1 to 9 estimating the chance a stock outperforms.

InvestGPT lets you ask for analysis in plain language, and an AI Stock Picker turns prompts into reusable screens. Smart Signals offers alerts and market movers, while an API provides data for backtests and portfolio tools. Coverage is concentrated on US equities, ETFs, crypto and major forex pairs, and the interface is English only. A free plan has limited credits and paid tiers add more. Nothing here is financial advice; check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Open the web app and sign up.
Look up a ticker and read its Kai Score.
Ask InvestGPT for an analysis or build a screen with the Stock Picker.
Set Smart Signals alerts for names you follow.
pros: Simple 1 to 9 rating for quick ranking
pricing_details: A free plan with limited research credits is described; Pro tiers add credits and features. Check the official site for current pricing.

faq.a: A 1 to 9 machine-learning rating of the probability a stock outperforms.
Only a limited international universe.
No; treat outputs as research input and do your own checks.

seo_title: Kavout: AI Stock Ranking and Research
seo_description: Kavout ranks stocks with the Kai Score and offers AI research, screens and signals, mainly for US markets.

name: Magnifi
tagline: Conversational investing platform for searching securities and tracking portfolios.
best_for: DIY retail investors who want guided research
description:
Magnifi is an AI investing platform from TIFIN. You search stocks, ETFs and mutual funds through a conversational interface, link accounts from other brokerages to view diversification and risk, and can place commission-free trades through its own brokerage.

Its marketplace lists over 15,000 securities, and planning tools cover goals, scenarios and portfolio comparison. One limit worth knowing: the in-house brokerage supports taxable accounts only, so IRAs and 401(k)s can be linked for analysis but not traded there. A free account covers browsing, education and trading, while a paid Magnifi Personal subscription unlocks the AI assistant and deeper analytics. This is not advice; check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Create an account.
Link your existing brokerage accounts for analysis.
Ask the assistant to find securities or compare funds.
Review risk and diversification before deciding on any trade.
cons: AI assistant needs a paid subscription

name: Numerai
tagline: Crowdsourced data science tournament that feeds a live hedge fund.
description:
Numerai is a crowdsourced hedge fund. Participants download obfuscated market data, train their own models and submit predictions weekly, and those submissions feed a live market-neutral fund.

The data is encrypted so raw identifiers stay hidden. Tournaments include Signals and Crypto, with a live leaderboard and a meta model that ensembles top submissions. Scoring uses tools such as era-based metrics and feature neutralization, and a Python API and CLI automate data pulls and submissions. Joining and downloading data is free; staking the NMR token is optional but required to earn payouts, and it carries financial risk. Check the official site for current rules.

Train a model in your own Python environment.
Submit predictions through the API or web.
Track scores on the leaderboard and decide whether to stake.

cons: Payouts require staking a crypto token
Needs real ML skills to do well
